title: Global molecular and serological evidence of dengue and chikungunya infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 158,608 tested participants.
abstract: Abstract Introduction Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) are Aedes-borne arboviruses with overlapping clinical manifestations, shared vectors, and substantial diagnostic challenges in co-endemic settings. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized published evidence on molecular detection, serological positivity, and DENV–CHIKV dual positivity/co-infection in human clinical, surveillance, and community-based study populations. Content Following PRISMA 2020 guidance, five bibliographic databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar) and supplementary grey-literature/preprint sources were searched for English-language studies published from 1 January 1980 to 31 December 2024. No prospective PROSPERO or OSF protocol registration was available. Eligible records reported extractable numerators and denominators for DENV and/or CHIKV in humans using recognized molecular or serological assays. A total of 196 studies comprising 158,608 tested or suspected participants were included in the extraction table. The pooled CHIKV estimate was 14.0 % (95 % CI: 12.0–16.4; I 2 =97.5 %), with molecular and serological estimates of 9.8 and 15.7 %, respectively. The pooled DENV estimate was 13.8 % (95 % CI: 10.9–17.3; I 2 =99.0 %), with molecular and serological estimates of 13.1 % (95 % CI: 7.9–21.0) and 14.3 % (95 % CI: 10.2–19.8), respectively. DENV–CHIKV dual positivity/co-infection was 52.9 % (95 % CI: 48.7–57.1) among studies that tested and reported both outcomes. Country-level estimates varied widely and should be interpreted as summaries of available studies rather than nationally representative burden estimates. Funnel-plot asymmetry was statistically significant in DENV analyses but not in the overall CHIKV analysis. Summary Available evidence indicates extensive but highly heterogeneous DENV and CHIKV positivity across selected clinical and surveillance populations. The pooled estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial between-study heterogeneity, diagnostic variability, outbreak-period sampling, and uneven geographic representation. Outlook The findings support integrated arboviral surveillance, multiplex diagnostics, and vector-control preparedness in co-endemic regions.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized published evidence on molecular detection, serological positivity, and DENV–CHIKV dual positivity/co-infection in human clinical, surveillance, and community-based study populations. Following PRISMA 2020 guidance, five bibliographic databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar) and supplementary grey-literature/preprint sources were searched for English-language studies published from 1 January 1980 to 31 December 2024. Eligible records reported extractable numerators and denominators for DENV and/or CHIKV in humans using recognized molecular or serological assays.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled DENV estimate was 13.8 % (95 % CI: 10.9–17.3; I 2 =99.0 %), with molecular and serological estimates of 13.1 % (95 % CI: 7.9–21.0) and 14.3 % (95 % CI: 10.2–19.8), respectively. The pooled CHIKV estimate was 14.0 % (95 % CI: 12.0–16.4; I 2 =97.5 %), with molecular and serological estimates of 9.8 and 15.7 %, respectively. DENV–CHIKV dual positivity/co-infection was 52.9 % (95 % CI: 48.7–57.1) among studies that tested and reported both outcomes. Available evidence indicates extensive but highly heterogeneous DENV and CHIKV positivity across selected clinical and surveillance populations.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The pooled estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial between-study heterogeneity, diagnostic variability, outbreak-period sampling, and uneven geographic representation. Country-level estimates varied widely and should be interpreted as summaries of available studies rather than nationally representative burden estimates. Funnel-plot asymmetry was statistically significant in DENV analyses but not in the overall CHIKV analysis. No prospective PROSPERO or OSF protocol registration was available.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings support integrated arboviral surveillance, multiplex diagnostics, and vector-control preparedness in co-endemic regions.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized molecular and serological evidence of dengue (DENV) and chikungunya (CHIKV) infections across 196 studies involving 158,608 participants. Pooled estimates showed DENV positivity at 13.8% (95% CI: 10.9–17.3) and CHIKV at 14.0% (95% CI: 12.0–16.4), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 >97%). Dual positivity reached 52.9% in co-endemic settings. Country-level estimates varied widely, reflecting diagnostic variability and uneven geographic representation. The findings underscore the need for integrated arboviral surveillance, multiplex diagnostics, and vector-control preparedness in regions where these viruses co-circulate.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 登革病毒 (DENV) 和基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 是伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒,具有重叠的临床表现、共同的 媒介 以及在共流行环境中的巨大诊断挑战。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这项系统综述和荟萃分析综合了已发表的关于人类临床、监测 和社区研究人群中分子检测、血清学阳性和 DENV-CHIKV 双重阳性/合并感染的证据。根据 PRISMA 2020 指南,对 5 个书目数据库(PubMed/MEDLINE、Scopus、Web of Science、ScienceDirect 和 Google Scholar)和补充灰色文献/预印本来源进行了搜索,查找 1980 年 1 月 1 日至 2024 年 12 月 31 日发表的英语研究。符合条件的记录报告了使用公认的分子或方法提取的人类 DENV 和/或 CHIKV 的分子和分母。血清学测定。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled DENV estimate was 13.8 % (95 % CI: 10.9–17.3; I 2 =99.0 %), with molecular and serological estimates of 13.1 % (95 % CI: 7.9–21.0) and 14.3 % (95 % CI: 10.2–19.8), respectively. DENV–CHIKV dual positivity/co-infection was 52.9 % (95 % CI: 48.7–57.1) among studies that tested and reported both outcomes. Available evidence indicates extensive but highly heterogeneous DENV and CHIKV positivity across selected clinical and surveillance populations.
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 由于研究间存在显着的异质性、诊断变异性、暴发 周期抽样以及不均匀的地理代表性,因此应谨慎解释汇总估计值。国家层面的估计差异很大,应解释为现有研究的总结,而不是具有全国代表性的负担估计。漏斗图不对称性在 DENV 分析中具有统计学显着性,但在整体 CHIKV 分析中并不显着。没有可用的前瞻性 PROSPERO 或 OSF 协议注册。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果支持在共同流行地区进行综合虫媒病毒 监测、多重诊断和 媒介 控制准备。

title_zh: 登革热和基孔肯雅热感染的全球分子和血清学证据:对 158,608 名测试参与者的系统回顾和荟萃分析。
source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) are Aedes-borne arboviruses with overlapping clinical manifestations, shared vectors, and substantial diagnostic challenges in co-endemic settings. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized published evidence on molecular detection, serological positivity, and DENV–CHIKV dual positivity/co-infection in human clinical, surveillance, and community-based study populations. Content Following PRISMA 2020 guidance, five bibliographic databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar) and supplementary grey-literature/preprint sources were searched for English-language studies published from 1 January 1980 to 31 December 2024. No prospective PROSPERO or OSF protocol registration was available. Eligible records reported extractable numerators and denominators for DENV and/or CHIKV in humans using recognized molecular or serological assays. A total of 196 studies comprising 158,608 tested or suspected participants were included in the extraction table. The pooled CHIKV estimate was 14.0 % (95 % CI: 12.0–16.4; I 2 =97.5 %), with molecular and serological estimates of 9.8 and 15.7 %, respectively. The pooled DENV estimate was 13.8 % (95 % CI: 10.9–17.3; I 2 =99.0 %), with molecular and serological estimates of 13.1 % (95 % CI: 7.9–21.0) and 14.3 % (95 % CI: 10.2–19.8), respectively. DENV–CHIKV dual positivity/co-infection was 52.9 % (95 % CI: 48.7–57.1) among studies that tested and reported both outcomes. Country-level estimates varied widely and should be interpreted as summaries of available studies rather than nationally representative burden estimates. Funnel-plot asymmetry was statistically significant in DENV analyses but not in the overall CHIKV analysis. Summary Available evidence indicates extensive but highly heterogeneous DENV and CHIKV positivity across selected clinical and surveillance populations. The pooled estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of substantial between-study heterogeneity, diagnostic variability, outbreak-period sampling, and uneven geographic representation. Outlook The findings support integrated arboviral surveillance, multiplex diagnostics, and vector-control preparedness in co-endemic regions.

title: Economic Impact of Dengue Virus in Mexico Over One Decade: A Systematic Literature Review (2010–2020)
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Dengue is a major mosquito‐borne viral disease worldwide, imposing significant healthcare burden on governments in countries where it is endemic, such as Mexico. This systematic review focused on studies reporting the cost of dengue in Mexico during 2010–2020. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first review discussing this topic in Mexico. We analysed all published direct costs associated with care, prevention, and surveillance, as well as indirect costs. Methods A comprehensive online search was conducted using Embase, MEDLINE, Evidence‐Based Medicine Reviews, SciELO, and LILACS. Articles reporting cost data published during 2010–2020 in English and Spanish were included. Reports from the National Ministry of Health and grey literature during the same period were also reviewed. Following the PICOS (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome and Study design) framework, articles reporting direct and indirect costs were included. The National Health Service Wales tool was used to assess the quality of the studies included. Results Seven articles fulfiled the inclusion criteria. All articles reported the nationwide cost of dengue, and three focused on specific Mexican states. The dengue‐related economic burden was substantial, peaking in 2013, with annual costs of $176.82 million (adjusted present value, $281.60 million). All the searches were verified in January 2023. Conclusions The economic burden of dengue in Mexico is high and is further impacted by outbreaks, resulting in significant costs to the healthcare system and productivity losses. The heterogeneity of the methodological approaches in the cost studies reviewed makes it a challenge to compare them.
journal: The International Journal of Health Planning and Management

title_zh: 登革病毒 十年来对墨西哥的经济影响:系统文献综述(2010-2020)
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background Dengue is a major mosquito‐borne viral disease worldwide, imposing significant healthcare burden on governments in countries where it is endemic, such as Mexico. This systematic review focused on studies reporting the cost of dengue in Mexico during 2010–2020. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first review discussing this topic in Mexico. We analysed all published direct costs associated with care, prevention, and surveillance, as well as indirect costs. Methods A comprehensive online search was conducted using Embase, MEDLINE, Evidence‐Based Medicine Reviews, SciELO, and LILACS. Articles reporting cost data published during 2010–2020 in English and Spanish were included. Reports from the National Ministry of Health and grey literature during the same period were also reviewed. Following the PICOS (Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome and Study design) framework, articles reporting direct and indirect costs were included. The National Health Service Wales tool was used to assess the quality of the studies included. Results Seven articles fulfiled the inclusion criteria. All articles reported the nationwide cost of dengue, and three focused on specific Mexican states. The dengue‐related economic burden was substantial, peaking in 2013, with annual costs of $176.82 million (adjusted present value, $281.60 million). All the searches were verified in January 2023. Conclusions The economic burden of dengue in Mexico is high and is further impacted by outbreaks, resulting in significant costs to the healthcare system and productivity losses. The heterogeneity of the methodological approaches in the cost studies reviewed makes it a challenge to compare them.

title: Study of the circulation of dengue, yellow fever, and West Nile viruses in Guinea: implications for achieving the health objectives of the Simandou 2040 program
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diseases such as dengue, yellow fever and West Nile virus, which are transmitted by arthropods, pose public health problems in tropical and subtropical regions. Like many West African countries, Guinea possesses all the conditions conducive to the circulation of these viruses. These include local ecology and climate, as well as the presence of vectors that transmit these viruses. Despite their medical importance, these viruses have received limited study, and up-to-date information on their circulation remains scarce. In this context, the present study examined the prevalence of these three arboviruses (DENV, YFV and WNV) in human and vector populations. METHODOLOGY: This study covered 18 Guinea prefectures, which are spread across the country's four ecological zones. The study was conducted from 27 May to 27 November 2024. In health centers selected in each prefecture, 5 ml samples of venous blood were collected from asymptomatic patients aged 1-90 years who had visited for consultations and had given their consent. Additionally, mosquitoes were collected via an "AMPLECTA MOSQUITO TRAP" light trap. Two ELISA tests were performed on the blood samples: the first for detection and the second for confirmation of the presence of these viruses in human serum. The mosquito samples were analyzed to determine diversity, and real-time PCR was employed to check for viral infection in the vectors following viral RNA extraction via the RIBO-prep AmpliSens® Kit. RESULTS: Serological evidence of exposure to all three viruses in the eighteen surveyed prefectures indicates their widespread distribution across the country. The highest seroprevalence of dengue virus antibodies was observed in N'Zerekore (43.9% [38.5-49.4%]), whereas the highest seroprevalence of yellow fever virus antibodies was recorded in Kankan Prefecture (54.7%; 95% CI: 41.5-67.3). In Forecariah, up to 53.0% (95% CI: 42.4-63.4) of participants were seropositive for West Nile virus antibodies. Seropositivity for these arboviruses was more frequently observed among adults. Higher seroprevalence of dengue and yellow fever antibodies was also observed among farmers and livestock breeders. No dengue or yellow fever infections were detected in the vectors, whereas the Culex quinquefasciatus population was found to be infected with WNV. CONCLUSION: This study provides serological evidence of exposure to dengue, yellow fever, and West Nile viruses across all the ecological regions of the Republic of Guinea. In addition, antibodies against these viruses were detected in human populations, and arbovirus-positive mosquito pools were identified during entomological investigations. Evidence of West Nile virus was also detected in mosquito pools containing Culex quinquefasciatus, suggesting a possible role of this species in the local transmission cycle. Adult farmers and livestock breeders appear to be at the greatest risk of contracting dengue and yellow fever. These results highlight the need for an integrated arbovirus surveillance system in Guinea. This system must combine serological surveillance with entomological surveys to support the public health objectives of the Simandou 2040 program.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines the circulation of dengue virus (DENV), yellow fever virus (YFV), and West Nile virus (WNV) in Guinea, focusing on their prevalence in human and vector populations across the country's four ecological zones. The central question is to assess the serological evidence of exposure to these arboviruses and identify risk factors for infection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a cross-sectional study conducted across 18 prefectures in Guinea from May to November 2024. Blood samples were collected from asymptomatic patients aged 1-90 years, and mosquitoes were collected using light traps. Serological testing was performed using ELISA, and mosquito samples were analyzed via real-time PCR. The study covered all four ecological zones of Guinea.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study confirms widespread serological evidence of exposure to DENV, YFV, and WNV across all ecological regions of Guinea. The highest seroprevalence of DENV was in N'Zerekore (43.9%), YFV in Kankan (54.7%), and WNV in Forecariah (53.0%). Adults, particularly farmers and livestock breeders, showed higher seropositivity for DENV and YFV. WNV was detected in Culex quinquefasciatus mosquitoes, suggesting its role in local transmission.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: No DENV or YFV infections were detected in vectors, despite human seropositivity, indicating gaps in understanding vector involvement for these viruses. The study does not address the absence of DENV/YFV in vectors or the potential for silent transmission cycles. Additionally, the lack of molecular confirmation for human infections beyond serology represents a methodological limitation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings highlight the need for an integrated arbovirus surveillance system in Guinea that combines serological surveillance with entomological surveys. This system is critical for supporting the public health objectives of the Simandou 2040 program. Targeted interventions should focus on high-risk groups such as farmers and livestock breeders.

analysis.summary_en: This study provides comprehensive evidence of dengue, yellow fever, and West Nile virus circulation in Guinea, with seroprevalence rates varying by region and occupation. While WNV was detected in Culex mosquitoes, the absence of DENV/YFV in vectors despite human infections warrants further investigation. The results underscore the need for integrated surveillance systems to guide public health interventions, particularly for high-risk adult populations involved in agriculture and livestock rearing.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述考察了几内亚 登革病毒 (DENV)、黄热病病毒 (YFV) 和西尼罗河病毒 (WNV) 的传播情况,重点关注其 患病率 在该国四个生态区的人类和 媒介 人群中的传播。核心问题是评估接触这些虫媒病毒的血清学证据并确定感染的危险因素。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一项于 2024 年 5 月至 11 月在几内亚 18 个省进行的横断面研究。从 1 岁至 90 岁的无症状患者中采集血液样本,并使用光诱捕器收集蚊子。使用 ELISA 进行血清学检测,并通过实时 PCR 分析蚊子样本。该研究涵盖了几内亚的所有四个生态区。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该研究证实了几内亚所有生态区域广泛暴露于 DENV、YFV 和 WNV 的血清学证据。DENV 最高的 血清流行率 位于 N'Zerekore (43.9%),YFV 位于 Kankan (54.7%),WNV 位于 Forecariah (53.0%)。成年人,特别是农民和牲畜饲养者,表现出较高的 DENV 和 YFV 血清阳性率。在致倦库蚊中检测到西尼罗河病毒,表明其在当地 传播 中的作用。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 尽管人类血清呈阳性,但在 媒介 中未检测到 DENV 或 YFV 感染,这表明对这些病毒参与 媒介 的了解存在差距。该研究并未解决 媒介 中 DENV/YFV 的缺失或沉默 传播 循环的可能性。此外,血清学 之外的人类感染缺乏分子证实,这代表了方法学上的局限性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调了几内亚需要一个综合虫媒病毒 监测 系统,将血清学 监测 与昆虫学调查相结合。该系统对于支持西芒杜 2040 计划的公共卫生目标至关重要。有针对性的干预措施应重点关注农民和畜牧业者等高风险群体。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述考察了几内亚 登革病毒 (DENV)、黄热病病毒 (YFV) 和西尼罗河病毒 (WNV) 的传播情况,重点关注其 患病率 在该国四个生态区的人类和 媒介 人群中的传播。核心问题是评估接触这些虫媒病毒的血清学证据并确定感染的危险因素。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一项于 2024 年 5 月至 11 月在几内亚 18 个省进行的横断面研究。从 1 岁至 90 岁的无症状患者中采集血液样本,并使用光诱捕器收集蚊子。使用 ELISA 进行血清学检测,并通过实时 PCR 分析蚊子样本。该研究涵盖了几内亚的所有四个生态区。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该研究证实了几内亚所有生态区域广泛暴露于 DENV、YFV 和 WNV 的血清学证据。DENV 最高的 血清流行率 位于 N'Zerekore (43.9%),YFV 位于 Kankan (54.7%),WNV 位于 Forecariah (53.0%)。成年人,特别是农民和牲畜饲养者,表现出较高的 DENV 和 YFV 血清阳性率。在致倦库蚊中检测到西尼罗河病毒,表明其在当地 传播 中的作用。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 尽管人类血清呈阳性,但在 媒介 中未检测到 DENV 或 YFV 感染,这表明对这些病毒参与 媒介 的了解存在差距。该研究并未解决 媒介 中 DENV/YFV 的缺失或沉默 传播 循环的可能性。此外,血清学 之外的人类感染缺乏分子证实,这代表了方法学上的局限性。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调了几内亚需要一个综合虫媒病毒 监测 系统,将血清学 监测 与昆虫学调查相结合。该系统对于支持西芒杜 2040 计划的公共卫生目标至关重要。有针对性的干预措施应重点关注农民和畜牧业者等高风险群体。

title: Molecular and Serological Surveillance of Dengue Virus and Vector Dynamics in the Highlands of Southwestern Saudi Arabia
abstract: Dengue fever is an emerging endemic disease in Saudi Arabia; however, important gaps remain regarding transmission dynamics, vector distribution, and serotype circulation in highland areas. This study primarily aimed to investigate dengue virus (DENV) infection and vector occurrence in the highland governorates of the Jazan region. A cross-sectional study enrolled 182 febrile patients tested using RT-qPCR, ELISA, RT-PCR-based serotyping, and rapid diagnostic tests. Concurrent entomological surveillance was conducted using CDC light traps, with morphological and molecular identification of Aedes aegypti. RT-qPCR confirmed acute DENV infection in 15.9% (29/182) of patients. Males showed significantly higher prevalence than females (23.4% vs. Primary infections accounted for 72.4%, while 27.6% were secondary. ELISA-NS1 demonstrated higher sensitivity (79.3%) and specificity (100%) than RDT-NS1 (58.6% and 99.4%), with stronger agreement with RT-qPCR (κ = 0.87 vs. IgG seropositivity (41.8%) suggests substantial prior exposure, likely reflecting ongoing endemicity rather than isolated outbreaks. DENV-2 predominated, followed by DENV-3, consistent with previously reported serotype patterns in Saudi Arabia. A total of 7,095 mosquitoes were collected, of which 20.9% were Ae. aegypti, detected year-round with peaks in August-September, likely associated with higher temperature and rainfall conditions. Monthly mosquito abundance correlated with dengue cases (r = 0.770; P = 0.006). These findings indicate that dengue transmission and vector presence extend into highland areas. Integrating molecular diagnostics with expanded vector surveillance is essential to strengthen dengue control beyond traditional endemic zones.

title: Design of a novel epitope-based tetravalent subunit vaccine against dengue virus: An immunoinformatic approach
abstract: Dengue imposes a profound global impact, with millions affected annually. Its transmission by Aedes mosquitoes poses significant challenges to combat, aggravated by urbanization and climate change. Despite efforts, no impeccable antiviral treatment exists to date, highlighting the urgency for a vaccine. Developing one encounters hurdles like the four distinctive serotypes of the virus and complex immune responses. In this study, we employed an immunoinformatics approach to design an epitope-based tetravalent subunit vaccine aimed at confronting all DENV serotypes. The study contemplates epitope prediction and screening, physicochemical assessment, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, immune simulations, and in silico cloning. The vaccine construct comprises human β-defensin 3 adjuvant and 23 epitopes joined with linkers. Notably, the vaccine has an antigenicity of 0.9319 with 97.35% population coverage worldwide. Molecular docking with toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) and TLR4 showed promising interactions with lowest energies of −1240.5 kJ/mol (76 members) and −1393.3 kJ/mol (40 members), respectively, exhibiting significant electrostatic, van dar Waals, and other interactions. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 200 nanoseconds revealed the vaccine to be stable and flexible with the receptors. The solvent accessibility and radius of gyration were also in suitable ranges. The three-dose vaccine regimen elicited a robust and durable multi-lineage immune response, characterized by stable B and T-cell memory, sustained surveillance, and high-titer antibody production (IgM/IgG) alongside a pro-inflammatory cytokine profile (IFN-γ and IL-2) for effective antigen clearance. These findings suggest that our vaccine outperforms any other Dengue vaccine developed to date. However, since this study was conducted through in silico methods, in vitro and in vivo validations are required to confirm the vaccine as a potential candidate for clinical trials.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue imposes a profound global impact, with millions affected annually, and despite efforts, no impeccable antiviral treatment exists to date, highlighting the urgency for a vaccine.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study employed an immunoinformatics approach to design an epitope-based tetravalent subunit vaccine aimed at confronting all DENV serotypes, with no specific population or clinical cohort involved.
analysis.methods: The study involved epitope prediction and screening, physicochemical assessment, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, immune simulations, and in silico cloning to evaluate the vaccine construct.
analysis.main_results: The vaccine construct showed an antigenicity of 0.9319 with 97.35% population coverage worldwide; molecular docking with TLR2 and TLR4 revealed promising interactions with lowest energies of −1240.5 kJ/mol and −1393.3 kJ/mol, respectively, and MD simulations confirmed stability and flexibility.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the vaccine outperforms any other Dengue vaccine developed to date, as evidenced by its robust immune response and high antigenicity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest potential for improved dengue prevention through a tetravalent subunit vaccine with broad population coverage and strong immune stimulation, though further validation is needed.

The vaccine includes human β-defensin 3 adjuvant and 23 epitopes, showing high antigenicity (0.9319) and 97.35% global population coverage. Molecular docking revealed strong interactions with TLR2 and TLR4, and MD simulations confirmed stability. The vaccine elicited robust immune responses with high-titer antibodies and pro-inflammatory cytokines. However, as the study was entirely computational, in vitro and in vivo validations are necessary before clinical trials.

title_zh: 针对 登革病毒 的新型基于表位的四价亚基 疫苗 的设计:一种免疫信息学方法
source_body_en: Dengue imposes a profound global impact, with millions affected annually. Its transmission by Aedes mosquitoes poses significant challenges to combat, aggravated by urbanization and climate change. Despite efforts, no impeccable antiviral treatment exists to date, highlighting the urgency for a vaccine. Developing one encounters hurdles like the four distinctive serotypes of the virus and complex immune responses. In this study, we employed an immunoinformatics approach to design an epitope-based tetravalent subunit vaccine aimed at confronting all DENV serotypes. The study contemplates epitope prediction and screening, physicochemical assessment, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, immune simulations, and in silico cloning. The vaccine construct comprises human β-defensin 3 adjuvant and 23 epitopes joined with linkers. Notably, the vaccine has an antigenicity of 0.9319 with 97.35% population coverage worldwide. Molecular docking with toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) and TLR4 showed promising interactions with lowest energies of −1240.5 kJ/mol (76 members) and −1393.3 kJ/mol (40 members), respectively, exhibiting significant electrostatic, van dar Waals, and other interactions. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 200 nanoseconds revealed the vaccine to be stable and flexible with the receptors. The solvent accessibility and radius of gyration were also in suitable ranges. The three-dose vaccine regimen elicited a robust and durable multi-lineage immune response, characterized by stable B and T-cell memory, sustained surveillance, and high-titer antibody production (IgM/IgG) alongside a pro-inflammatory cytokine profile (IFN-γ and IL-2) for effective antigen clearance. These findings suggest that our vaccine outperforms any other Dengue vaccine developed to date. However, since this study was conducted through in silico methods, in vitro and in vivo validations are required to confirm the vaccine as a potential candidate for clinical trials.

title: Comparative Performance of Mechanistic, Statistical, and Hybrid Models of Forecasting Dengue Fever Incidence in Somalia. A Retrospective Time Series Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Dengue fever is a growing menace in Somalia, a climate change prone region with a weak healthcare system. An imperative of public health is effective forecasting models. This paper will provide a detailed comparative analysis comparing mechanistic, statistical, and hybrid models in order to find the best forecasting model to use in this data‐sparse situation of dengue fever. Methods We utilized raw reported annual incidence data of dengue (1990–2021, N = 32) obtained from Our World in Data. Due to the lack of standardized case definitions and high under‐reporting inherent to Somalia's surveillance system, forecasts represent the projected reported burden rather than true infection rates. The data was divided into a training and a testing set (1990–2016 and 2017–2021, respectively). We tested a mechanistic Susceptible‐Infected‐Recovered (SIR) model, 8 single time series models (ARIMA, ETS, TBATS, and NNAR), and 12 hybrids using an averaging ensemble strategy. Findings Although the time series models (individually) offered the basics of predictive power, the hybrid ARIMA‐TBATS model was the most successful and it surpassed the other models. It performed the highest accuracy statistics on the testing data with a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 6.49% and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 663.81 and outperformed the best single model (TBATS) which had a MAPE of 7.14%. The basic reproduction number (R0) calculated by the SIR model was 1.015 which shows that the disease is endemic. Conclusion This paper concludes that the ARIMA‐TBATS hybrid should be the most empirically effective tool out of the ones considered when planning to forecast dengue in Somalia. Real‐World Application: This ARIMA‐TBATS framework is designed to serve as the mathematical engine for a National Dengue Early Warning System (DEWS) in Somalia, allowing public health officials to physically preempt outbreaks by routing medical supplies, mobilizing fumigation teams, and distributing bed nets to high‐risk zones months before peak incidence occurs.

title_zh: 索马里 登革热 发病率 预测的机械、统计和混合模型的比较性能。回顾性时间序列分析
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Dengue fever is a growing menace in Somalia, a climate change prone region with a weak healthcare system. An imperative of public health is effective forecasting models. This paper will provide a detailed comparative analysis comparing mechanistic, statistical, and hybrid models in order to find the best forecasting model to use in this data‐sparse situation of dengue fever. Methods We utilized raw reported annual incidence data of dengue (1990–2021, N = 32) obtained from Our World in Data. Due to the lack of standardized case definitions and high under‐reporting inherent to Somalia's surveillance system, forecasts represent the projected reported burden rather than true infection rates. The data was divided into a training and a testing set (1990–2016 and 2017–2021, respectively). We tested a mechanistic Susceptible‐Infected‐Recovered (SIR) model, 8 single time series models (ARIMA, ETS, TBATS, and NNAR), and 12 hybrids using an averaging ensemble strategy. Findings Although the time series models (individually) offered the basics of predictive power, the hybrid ARIMA‐TBATS model was the most successful and it surpassed the other models. It performed the highest accuracy statistics on the testing data with a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 6.49% and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 663.81 and outperformed the best single model (TBATS) which had a MAPE of 7.14%. The basic reproduction number (R0) calculated by the SIR model was 1.015 which shows that the disease is endemic. Conclusion This paper concludes that the ARIMA‐TBATS hybrid should be the most empirically effective tool out of the ones considered when planning to forecast dengue in Somalia. Real‐World Application: This ARIMA‐TBATS framework is designed to serve as the mathematical engine for a National Dengue Early Warning System (DEWS) in Somalia, allowing public health officials to physically preempt outbreaks by routing medical supplies, mobilizing fumigation teams, and distributing bed nets to high‐risk zones months before peak incidence occurs.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景和目标 登革热 对索马里来说是一个日益严重的威胁,索马里是一个气候变化易发地区,医疗保健系统薄弱。公共卫生的当务之急是有效的预测模型。本文将对机械模型、统计模型和混合模型进行详细的比较分析,以便找到在 登革热 数据稀疏的情况下使用的最佳预测模型。方法 我们利用从“我们的数据世界”获得的登革热年度 发病率 原始报告数据(1990-2021 年,N = 32)。由于缺乏标准化病例定义以及索马里 监测 系统固有的高漏报率,预测代表的是预计报告的负担,而不是真实的感染率。数据分为训练集和测试集(分别为 1990-2016 年和 2017-2021 年)。我们使用平均集成策略测试了机械感染-感染-恢复 (SIR) 模型、8 个单一时间序列模型(ARIMA、ETS、TBATS 和 NNAR)以及 12 个混合模型。研究结果 虽然时间序列模型(单独)提供了预测能力的基础知识,但混合 ARIMA-TBATS 模型是最成功的,并且超越了其他模型。它对测试数据进行了最高精度的统计,平均绝对百分比误差(MAPE)为6.49%,均方根误差(RMSE)为663.81,并且优于MAPE为7.14%的最佳单一模型(TBATS)。SIR模型计算的基本再生数(R0)为1.015,表明该病具有地方性流行。结论 本文的结论是,在计划预测索马里登革热时,ARIMA-TBATS 混合工具应该是考虑的工具中经验最有效的工具。现实世界应用:该 ARIMA-TBATS 框架旨在作为索马里国家登革热早期预警系统 (DEWS) 的数学引擎,允许公共卫生官员在 发病率 高峰出现前几个月,通过运送医疗用品、动员熏蒸小组以及向高危地区分发蚊帐来抢占 暴发。

title: Antibody Responses in Pediatric Dengue Indicate Emergence and Co‐Circulation of DENV‐3 Genotypes I and III in Myanmar and Orthoflavivirus Cross‐Reactivity
abstract: ABSTRACT Dengue virus (DENV) remains a major public health concern in Southeast Asia, disproportionately affecting children. In Myanmar, DENV‐3 Genotype III predominated before 2017, with Genotype I emerging thereafter. To assess the impact of this emergence on antibody responses, we analyzed paired acute and convalescent serum samples from 38 pediatric dengue patients collected between 2017 and 2019 alongside archived 2004 samples. Neutralization and in vitro antibody‐dependent enhancement (ADE) were assessed against DENV‐3 Genotypes I and III and other serotypes, with cross‐reactivity analysis to Zika and Japanese encephalitis viruses. Samples from 2004 showed reduced neutralization and higher ADE for Genotype I, consistent with its absence at the time. In contrast, 2017–2019 samples exhibited comparable neutralization for both genotypes, with genotype‐ and year‐dependent ADE differences, indicating that Genotype I emergence was associated with evolving functional antibody profiles. Hence, providing immunological evidence for continued co‐circulation of DENV‐3 Genotypes I and III in Myanmar. Future prospective pediatric cohort studies with continuous surveillance of circulating orthoflaviviruses and their genotypes, are essential to elucidate how pre‐existing dengue immunity shapes genotype emergence and cross‐orthoflavivirus immunity in endemic regions.

title: Immune Modulatory Therapy for Severe Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever in a Patient With Mitochondrial Complex I Deficiency: A Case Report
abstract: ABSTRACT Dengue virus (DENV) poses a serious global health challenge, particularly in cases of dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF). Patients with preexisting mitochondrial disorders may be at increased risk for complications due to the specific impact of DENV on mitochondrial‐dependent cellular processes and immune function. We describe a 16‐year‐old male with known mitochondrial complex I deficiency caused by a homozygous likely pathogenic variant in NDUFV1 who subsequently developed DHF. His illness was marked by rapidly worsening weakness, respiratory distress, intracranial hemorrhage, and seizures. His clinical course was further complicated by encephalitis, arachnoiditis, and myelitis requiring extensive immunomodulation. He received corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), and plasma exchange (PLEX), which led to improvement and partial recovery of functional status. This case highlights several rare complications of dengue fever, the impact of DENV on mitochondrial function, and underscores the complexity of managing infectious diseases in individuals with underlying mitochondrial disorders.
journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A

title: Characterization of vaccine viremia, attenuation reversion, and safety: Combined results from the TAK-003 dengue vaccine clinical development program.
abstract: Live-attenuated vaccines can replicate for a transient period post-vaccination and may be associated with symptoms resembling natural infection. The tetravalent dengue vaccine, TAK-003, has undergone extensive preclinical assessment to investigate vaccine RNAemia, viremia, genetic stability, and transmissibility. Here, we investigated the presence of vaccine RNAemia, attenuation loci reversions, and their association with viral-syndrome-like adverse events (AEs) in participants throughout the clinical development program. TAK-003 RNA positive serum samples were evaluated for viral replication and sequenced for reversions. Safety data (solicited AEs within 7/14 days; unsolicited AEs within 28 days) were assessed from a pooled phase 1/2 trial analysis. Participants who experienced febrile illness within 30 days post vaccination in the pivotal phase 3 DEN-301 trial and the phase 2 DEN-313 trial were tested for RNAemia and evaluated for AEs. TAK-003 RNAemia was detected in 441/805 (54.8%) of vaccinees (seronegative: 67.0%; seropositive: 33.0%) in the pooled analysis and in 39 participants with febrile illness from the DEN-301/DEN-313 trials (from 1022 febrile illnesses investigated). RNAemia peaked during the second week post-vaccination and mostly occurred after first dose. Although all four dengue virus (DENV) components were detected, RNAemia was most commonly due to DENV-2. 69 single locus reversions were detected; AEs reported in participants with reversions were generally non-serious, and not indicative of increased symptom severity. Pain at injection site (without RNAemia = 42.0%; RNAemia = 46.8%) and headache (without RNAemia = 36.6%; RNAemia = 37.6%) were the most frequently reported solicited AEs. Incidences of pain, erythema, rash, arthralgia, and fatigue were higher in participants with RNAemia. The incidence of unsolicited AEs was higher in participants with RNAemia (62.4%) than without (52.0%). In the DEN-301/DEN-313 analysis, participants with febrile illness showed a similar pattern of symptoms with and without RNAemia. The presence of RNAemia was associated with transient, mild-to-moderate symptoms, resembling natural infection, which were also observed in the absence of RNAemia.

The tetravalent dengue vaccine, TAK-003, has undergone extensive preclinical assessment to investigate vaccine RNAemia, viremia, genetic stability, and transmissibility. Here, we investigated the presence of vaccine RNAemia, attenuation loci reversions, and their association with viral-syndrome-like adverse events (AEs) in participants throughout the clinical development program. TAK-003 RNA positive serum samples were evaluated for viral replication and sequenced for reversions. Safety data (solicited AEs within 7/14 days; unsolicited AEs within 28 days) were assessed from a pooled phase 1/2 trial analysis. Participants who experienced febrile illness within 30 days post vaccination in the pivotal phase 3 DEN-301 trial and the phase 2 DEN-313 trial were tested for RNAemia and evaluated for AEs. TAK-003 RNAemia was detected in 441/805 (54.8%) of vaccinees (seronegative: 67.0%; seropositive: 33.0%) in the pooled analysis and in 39 participants with febrile illness from the DEN-301/DEN-313 trials (from 1022 febrile illnesses investigated). RNAemia peaked during the second week post-vaccination and mostly occurred after first dose. Although all four dengue virus (DENV) components were detected, RNAemia was most commonly due to DENV-2. 69 single locus reversions were detected; AEs reported in participants with reversions were generally non-serious, and not indicative of increased symptom severity. Pain at injection site (without RNAemia = 42.0%; RNAemia = 46.8%) and headache (without RNAemia = 36.6%; RNAemia = 37.6%) were the most frequently reported solicited AEs. Incidences of pain, erythema, rash, arthralgia, and fatigue were higher in participants with RNAemia. The incidence of unsolicited AEs was higher in participants with RNAemia (62.4%) than without (52.0%). In the DEN-301/DEN-313 analysis, participants with febrile illness showed a similar pattern of symptoms with and without RNAemia. The presence of RNAemia was associated with transient, mild-to-moderate symptoms, resembling natural infection, which were also observed in the absence of RNAemia.

abstract_zh: 减毒活 疫苗 可以在 疫苗接种 后短暂复制,并可能与类似自然感染的症状相关。四价登革热 疫苗(TAK-003)已接受广泛的临床前评估,以研究 疫苗 RNA 血症、病毒血症、遗传稳定性和传播性。在这里,我们研究了整个临床开发项目参与者中 疫苗 RNAemia 的存在、减毒基因座逆转及其与病毒综合征样不良事件 (AE) 的关联。对 TAK-003 RNA 阳性血清样本进行病毒复制评估和逆转测序。安全性数据(7/14 天内主动发生的 AE;28 天内主动主动发生的 AE)通过汇总 1/2 期试验分析进行评估。在关键的 3 期 DEN-301 试验和 2 期 DEN-313 试验中,在 疫苗接种 后 30 天内出现发热性疾病的参与者接受了 RNA 血症检测并评估了 AE。在汇总分析中,441/805 (54.8%) 名 疫苗 患者(血清阴性:67.0%;血清阳性:33.0%)以及 DEN-301/DEN-313 试验(调查的 1022 例发热性疾病)中的 39 名发热性疾病参与者中检测到 TAK-003 RNA 血症。RNA 血症在 疫苗接种 后第二周达到峰值,并且大多发生在第一次给药后。尽管检测到所有四种 登革病毒 (DENV) 成分,但 RNAemia 最常见的是 DENV-2。检测到 69 个单基因座回复;逆转参与者报告的 AE 一般不严重,并不表明症状严重程度增加。注射部位疼痛(无 RNA 血症 = 42.0%;RNA 血症 = 46.8%)和头痛(无 RNA 血症 = 36.6%;RNA 血症 = 37.6%)是最常报告的引起的 AE。RNA 血症参与者的疼痛、红斑、皮疹、关节痛和疲劳 发病率 较高。患有 RNA 血症的参与者 (62.4%) 中主动出现的 AE 的 发病率 高于未患有 RNA 血症的参与者 (52.0%)。在 DEN-301/DEN-313 分析中,患有发热性疾病的参与者在有或没有 RNA 血症的情况下表现出相似的症状模式。RNA 血症的存在与短暂的轻度至中度症状相关,类似于自然感染,在不存在 RNA 血症的情况下也观察到这种情况。

title: Computational insights into dengue virus envelope protein triggered membrane fusion process
abstract: The membrane fusion process initiated by the Envelope (E) protein of the Dengue virus (DENV) is a critical step in viral entry into host cells, yet its molecular mechanism remains only partially understood. Here, we employ a combination of all-atom and coarse-grained molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model the insertion and progression of the dengue virus Envelope protein into a lipid bilayer, capturing key stages of the membrane fusion event. All-atom simulations provide atomistic insight into initial protein-lipid interactions, time evolution of protein-lipid contacts and conformational rearrangements of the E protein fusion loop, while coarse-grained models enable observation of long-timescale membrane remodeling events, such as curvature generation. Structural and dynamic analyses reveal how the E protein perturbs the membrane architecture, promoting negative curvature in the target membrane at the site of entry and positive curvature in adjoining regions that resemble early hemifusion intermediates. These results support the hypothesis that the fusion loop acts as a membrane anchor, and that coordinated protein insertion and tilting are essential for catalyzing membrane merger. This study offers a detailed molecular view of dengue virus fusion initiation and demonstrates the value of multiscale simulation approaches in studying complex membrane-protein interactions.
journal: Journal of Biomolecular Structure and Dynamics

abstract_original: The membrane fusion process initiated by the Envelope (E) protein of the Dengue virus (DENV) is a critical step in viral entry into host cells, yet its molecular mechanism remains only partially understood. Here, we employ a combination of all-atom and coarse-grained molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model the insertion and progression of the dengue virus Envelope protein into a lipid bilayer, capturing key stages of the membrane fusion event. All-atom simulations provide atomistic insight into initial protein-lipid interactions, time evolution of protein-lipid contacts and conformational rearrangements of the E protein fusion loop, while coarse-grained models enable observation of long-timescale membrane remodeling events, such as curvature generation. Structural and dynamic analyses reveal how the E protein perturbs the membrane architecture, promoting negative curvature in the target membrane at the site of entry and positive curvature in adjoining regions that resemble early hemifusion intermediates. These results support the hypothesis that the fusion loop acts as a membrane anchor, and that coordinated protein insertion and tilting are essential for catalyzing membrane merger. This study offers a detailed molecular view of dengue virus fusion initiation and demonstrates the value of multiscale simulation approaches in studying complex membrane-protein interactions.
title_original: Computational insights into dengue virus envelope protein triggered membrane fusion process

analysis.summary_en: Dengue virus entry relies on membrane fusion mediated by the Envelope (E) protein, a process whose molecular details are incompletely understood. To address this gap, the researchers used both all‐atom and coarse‐grained molecular dynamics simulations to model how the E protein inserts into and remodels a lipid bilayer. The simulations showed that the protein induces negative curvature at the site of entry and positive curvature in surrounding areas, forming structures reminiscent of early hemifusion intermediates. These observations support the idea that the fusion loop serves as a membrane anchor and that coordinated insertion and tilting of the protein are crucial for membrane merger. By delivering a high‐resolution, multiscale view of the fusion mechanism, the work highlights the utility of computational approaches for elucidating viral entry and may guide future antiviral strategies targeting this step.

abstract_zh: 由 登革病毒 (DENV) 的包膜 (E) 蛋白启动的膜融合过程是病毒进入 宿主 细胞的关键步骤,但其分子机制仍然只有部分了解。在这里,我们结合使用全原子和粗粒度分子动力学 (MD) 模拟来模拟 登革病毒 包膜蛋白插入和进展到脂质双层的过程,捕获膜融合事件的关键阶段。全原子模拟提供了对初始蛋白质-脂质相互作用、蛋白质-脂质接触的时间 进化 以及 E 蛋白融合环的构象重排的原子洞察,而粗粒度模型可以观察长时间尺度的膜重塑事件,例如曲率生成。结构和动态分析揭示了 E 蛋白如何扰乱膜结构,促进进入部位目标膜的负曲率和类似于早期半融合中间体的相邻区域的正曲率。这些结果支持这样的假设:融合环充当膜锚,并且协调的蛋白质插入和倾斜对于催化膜合并至关重要。这项研究提供了 登革病毒 融合起始的详细分子视图,并证明了多尺度模拟方法在研究复杂膜蛋白相互作用中的价值。

title: Substance P and NK‐1R in Dengue: A First Serological Investigation
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Dengue fever lacks reliable biomarkers to explain its complex pathophysiology. Substance P (SP) and its receptor, the Neurokinin‐1 receptor (NK1R), known regulators of inflammation and vascular permeability in viral infections, may play a role in dengue but remain unexplored. Aim/Objective To investigate the levels of SP and NK1R in serum samples of diagnosed dengue patients. Methods Participants were selected from a pool of diagnosed dengue fever patients using a convenience sampling technique ( n = 40), along with a control group of healthy individuals ( n = 12). Serum samples were collected, and SP and NK1R levels were measured using enzyme‐linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Complete blood count (CBC) parameters were also evaluated. Results The mean NK1R levels in the control and case groups were 2.681 ± 3.147 and 0.57 ± 0.131, respectively. NK1R levels were significantly lower in dengue patients compared with controls ( p < 0.0001). SP levels did not differ significantly between male and female dengue patients (Mann–Whitney U = 85, p = 0.899). Conclusion NK1R may be associated with dengue pathogenesis through its potential involvement in vascular permeability, immune activation, and cytokine responses. These findings suggest a possible connection between NK1R and the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying dengue infection.

title: Uncovering dengue serotype-specific transmission, cross-reactivity, and immune profiles from cross-sectional serosurveys
abstract: Abstract Dengue remains a growing global health concern, with four co-circulating serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4). Cross-sectional serosurveys are essential for inferring past transmission and population immunity, but serotype-specific interpretation is constrained by antibody cross-reactivity across serotypes. Here, we developed a novel modelling framework to jointly infer serotype-specific force of infection (FOI) and cross-reactivity from cross-sectional serosurveys. The model is flexible to data granularity, functioning with binary serostatus alone or combined with quantitative titres. In simulations, the model effectively recovered FOI and cross-reactivity across varying endemicity, sampling designs, and sample age coverage. Applied to annual cross-sectional serosurveys in Vietnam (2013-2017), the model estimated serotype-specific FOI patterns comparable in overall magnitude to analysis requiring supplementary longitudinal post-infection antibody measurements, which are difficult to collect. We further identified higher DENV-3 transmission intensity than previously estimated. Our estimates revealed asymmetric cross-reactivity between infecting and heterologous antibody-response serotypes after primary infections, and high cross-reactivity after post-primary infections. We reconstructed population immune profiles by age, time, serotype, and past infection number, resolving single-serotype and multi-serotype exposure histories not directly distinguishable from observed seroprevalence. Our estimates showed that susceptibility to secondary infection in Vietnam peaked at approximately age 10 for each serotype, and averaged ∼25% for DENV-1 to DENV-3 and ∼30% for DENV-4 among individuals aged 1-30 years. Additionally, incorporating titres enabled individual-level infection-history inference and revealed exposure-history signals in titre profiles despite extensive cross-reactivity. These findings show that improved modelling can substantially expand the information recoverable from cross-sectional serology, strengthening the public-health utility of serosurveys for risk assessment, burden estimation, and vaccination planning.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on dengue virus (DENV-1 to DENV-4) and its transmission, cross-reactivity, and immune profiles using cross-sectional serosurveys. The central question is how to infer serotype-specific force of infection (FOI) and cross-reactivity from cross-sectional data, addressing limitations in traditional methods.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a review article published in medRxiv in 2026. The authors developed a novel modeling framework to jointly infer serotype-specific FOI and cross-reactivity from cross-sectional serosurveys. The model was tested in simulations and applied to annual serosurveys in Vietnam (2013-2017).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The model effectively recovered FOI and cross-reactivity across varying endemicity and sampling designs. Applied to Vietnam data, it estimated serotype-specific FOI patterns comparable to longitudinal methods and identified higher DENV-3 transmission intensity. Asymmetric cross-reactivity was observed between infecting and heterologous antibody-response serotypes, with high cross-reactivity after post-primary infections.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report specific controversies but highlights that serotype-specific interpretation of cross-sectional serosurveys is constrained by antibody cross-reactivity. The model addresses this gap, but the review does not discuss limitations in data granularity or regional applicability beyond Vietnam.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Improved modeling can expand information recoverable from cross-sectional serology, strengthening public-health utility for risk assessment, burden estimation, and vaccination planning. The model enables reconstruction of population immune profiles and individual-level infection-history inference, despite cross-reactivity challenges.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 登革病毒(DENV-1 至 DENV-4)及其 传播、交叉反应性和使用横断面血清调查的免疫特征。核心问题是如何从横截面数据推断血清型特异性感染力(FOI)和交叉反应性,解决传统方法的局限性。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是 2026 年发表在 medRxiv 上的一篇综述文章。作者开发了一种新颖的建模框架,可以从横断面血清调查中联合推断血清型特异性 FOI 和交叉反应性。该模型经过了模拟测试,并应用于越南的年度血清调查(2013-2017 年)。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该模型有效地恢复了不同流行病和抽样设计的 FOI 和交叉反应性。应用到越南数据,它估计了与纵向方法相当的血清型特异性 FOI 模式,并确定了更高的 DENV-3 传播 强度。在感染血清型和异源抗体反应血清型之间观察到不对称交叉反应性,在初次感染后具有高交叉反应性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有报告具体的争议,但强调横断面血清调查的血清型特异性解释受到抗体交叉反应性的限制。该模型解决了这一差距,但审查并未讨论数据粒度或越南以外区域适用性的限制。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 改进的模型可以扩展从横截面 血清学 中恢复的信息,加强风险评估、负担估计和 疫苗接种 规划的公共卫生实用性。尽管存在交叉反应的挑战,该模型仍然能够重建群体免疫特征和个体水平的感染史推断。

title_zh: 通过横断面血清调查揭示登革热血清型特异性 传播、交叉反应性和免疫特征
source_body_en: Abstract Dengue remains a growing global health concern, with four co-circulating serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4). Cross-sectional serosurveys are essential for inferring past transmission and population immunity, but serotype-specific interpretation is constrained by antibody cross-reactivity across serotypes. Here, we developed a novel modelling framework to jointly infer serotype-specific force of infection (FOI) and cross-reactivity from cross-sectional serosurveys. The model is flexible to data granularity, functioning with binary serostatus alone or combined with quantitative titres. In simulations, the model effectively recovered FOI and cross-reactivity across varying endemicity, sampling designs, and sample age coverage. Applied to annual cross-sectional serosurveys in Vietnam (2013-2017), the model estimated serotype-specific FOI patterns comparable in overall magnitude to analysis requiring supplementary longitudinal post-infection antibody measurements, which are difficult to collect. We further identified higher DENV-3 transmission intensity than previously estimated. Our estimates revealed asymmetric cross-reactivity between infecting and heterologous antibody-response serotypes after primary infections, and high cross-reactivity after post-primary infections. We reconstructed population immune profiles by age, time, serotype, and past infection number, resolving single-serotype and multi-serotype exposure histories not directly distinguishable from observed seroprevalence. Our estimates showed that susceptibility to secondary infection in Vietnam peaked at approximately age 10 for each serotype, and averaged ∼25% for DENV-1 to DENV-3 and ∼30% for DENV-4 among individuals aged 1-30 years. Additionally, incorporating titres enabled individual-level infection-history inference and revealed exposure-history signals in titre profiles despite extensive cross-reactivity. These findings show that improved modelling can substantially expand the information recoverable from cross-sectional serology, strengthening the public-health utility of serosurveys for risk assessment, burden estimation, and vaccination planning.
abstract_zh: 摘要 登革热仍然是一个日益严重的全球健康问题,有四种共同流行的血清型(DENV-1 至 DENV-4)。横断面血清调查对于推断过去的 传播 和群体免疫力至关重要,但血清型特异性解释受到血清型间抗体交叉反应性的限制。在这里,我们开发了一种新颖的建模框架,可以从横断面血清调查中联合推断血清型特异性感染力(FOI)和交叉反应性。该模型对数据粒度非常灵活,可单独使用二元血清状态或与定量滴度结合使用。在模拟中,该模型有效地恢复了不同流行情况、抽样设计和样本年龄覆盖范围的 FOI 和交叉反应性。该模型应用于越南的年度横断面血清调查(2013-2017),估计的血清型特异性 FOI 模式在总体规模上与需要补充纵向感染后抗体测量的分析相当,而这些分析很难收集。我们进一步确定了 DENV-3 传播 强度比之前估计的更高。我们的估计揭示了初次感染后感染血清型和异源抗体反应血清型之间的不对称交叉反应性,以及初次感染后的高交叉反应性。我们根据年龄、时间、血清型和既往感染数量重建了群体免疫特征,解决了与观察到的 血清流行率 无法直接区分的单血清型和多血清型暴露史。我们的估计显示,越南每种血清型的继发感染易感性在大约 10 岁时达到峰值,在 1-30 岁的个体中,DENV-1 至 DENV-3 的平均感染率约为 25%,DENV-4 的平均感染率约为 30%。此外,尽管存在广泛的交叉反应,但合并滴度可以实现个体水平的感染史推断,并在滴度曲线中揭示暴露史信号。这些发现表明,改进的模型可以大大扩展从横截面 血清学 中可恢复的信息,加强血清调查在风险评估、负担估计和 疫苗接种 规划方面的公共卫生效用。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 登革病毒(DENV-1 至 DENV-4)及其 传播、交叉反应性和使用横断面血清调查的免疫特征。核心问题是如何从横截面数据推断血清型特异性感染力(FOI)和交叉反应性,解决传统方法的局限性。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是 2026 年发表在 medRxiv 上的一篇综述文章。作者开发了一种新颖的建模框架,可以从横断面血清调查中联合推断血清型特异性 FOI 和交叉反应性。该模型经过了模拟测试,并应用于越南的年度血清调查(2013-2017 年)。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该模型有效地恢复了不同流行病和抽样设计的 FOI 和交叉反应性。应用到越南数据,它估计了与纵向方法相当的血清型特异性 FOI 模式,并确定了更高的 DENV-3 传播 强度。在感染血清型和异源抗体反应血清型之间观察到不对称交叉反应性,在初次感染后具有高交叉反应性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有报告具体的争议,但强调横断面血清调查的血清型特异性解释受到抗体交叉反应性的限制。该模型解决了这一差距,但审查并未讨论数据粒度或越南以外区域适用性的限制。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 改进的模型可以扩展从横截面 血清学 中恢复的信息,加强风险评估、负担估计和 疫苗接种 规划的公共卫生实用性。尽管存在交叉反应的挑战,该模型仍然能够重建群体免疫特征和个体水平的感染史推断。

title: Immature platelet fraction predicts differential platelet recovery trajectories in dengue fever: A longitudinal analysis
abstract: Summary Dengue commonly causes thrombocytopenia, but platelet count alone may not reflect marrow thrombopoiesis. Immature platelet fraction (IPF) is a potential marker of platelet regeneration, though longitudinal data are limited. We thus aimed to evaluate whether Day 1 IPF predicts subsequent platelet recovery trajectory and to describe longitudinal trends in clinical, biochemical and platelet indices. This was a retrospective longitudinal analytical study conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Western Maharashtra, India. Six hundred and sixty‐seven patients with confirmed dengue, with platelet count, IPF and World Health Organization (WHO) classification recorded on Day 1, with follow‐up at Day 3 and 5. Log‐transformed platelet counts at Day 3 and Day 5 were analysed using generalized least squares regression. Longitudinal changes were assessed using the Friedman test. Median age was 31 years, with 81.4% males. Platelet counts declined from 118 to 98 × 10 9 /L ( p = 0.0017), while IPF increased from 9.7% to 12.9% ( p < 0.0001). Higher baseline IPF predicted faster platelet recovery ( p < 0.0001). Continued platelet decline at Day 5 was lower in the high‐IPF group than the low‐IPF group (28.6% vs. 47.8%; Kruskal–Wallis p = 0.013). We thus conclude that IPF is a dynamic biomarker that predicts platelet recovery trajectory in dengue.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热通常会导致血小板减少,但仅血小板计数可能无法反映骨髓血小板生成。本研究旨在评估第 1 天未成熟血小板分数 (IPF) 是否可以预测随后的血小板恢复轨迹,并描述临床、生化和血小板指数的纵向趋势。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项在印度西马哈拉施特拉邦一家三级护理医院进行的回顾性纵向分析研究。667 名确诊登革热患者,在第 1 天记录血小板计数、IPF 和世界卫生组织 (WHO) 分类,并在第 3 天和第 5 天进行随访。

title_zh: 未成熟血小板分数预测 登革热 中不同的血小板恢复轨迹:纵向分析
source_body_en: Summary Dengue commonly causes thrombocytopenia, but platelet count alone may not reflect marrow thrombopoiesis. Immature platelet fraction (IPF) is a potential marker of platelet regeneration, though longitudinal data are limited. We thus aimed to evaluate whether Day 1 IPF predicts subsequent platelet recovery trajectory and to describe longitudinal trends in clinical, biochemical and platelet indices. This was a retrospective longitudinal analytical study conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Western Maharashtra, India. Six hundred and sixty‐seven patients with confirmed dengue, with platelet count, IPF and World Health Organization (WHO) classification recorded on Day 1, with follow‐up at Day 3 and 5. Log‐transformed platelet counts at Day 3 and Day 5 were analysed using generalized least squares regression. Longitudinal changes were assessed using the Friedman test. Median age was 31 years, with 81.4% males. Platelet counts declined from 118 to 98 × 10 9 /L ( p = 0.0017), while IPF increased from 9.7% to 12.9% ( p < 0.0001). Higher baseline IPF predicted faster platelet recovery ( p < 0.0001). Continued platelet decline at Day 5 was lower in the high‐IPF group than the low‐IPF group (28.6% vs. 47.8%; Kruskal–Wallis p = 0.013). We thus conclude that IPF is a dynamic biomarker that predicts platelet recovery trajectory in dengue.

title: A tiered molecular surveillance framework linking rapid dengue detection to genomic epidemiology in Senegal.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Arboviral surveillance in Africa is limited by fragmented diagnostic capacity and insufficient integration of molecular detection with genomic epidemiology, particularly in settings where dengue (DENV), Zika (ZIKV), and chikungunya (CHIKV) viruses co-circulate and present with overlapping clinical syndromes. METHODS: We conducted a molecular surveillance study across multiple regions in Senegal, including samples collected from 367 individuals with febrile or non-febrile illness. A tiered workflow was implemented using multiplex reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) screening for DENV, ZIKV, and CHIKV, performed on a combination of individually tested samples (n=43) and pooled samples (three individuals per pool). DENV RT-qPCR-positive samples were further characterized by reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification (RT-RPA) serotyping and genomic sequencing. FINDINGS: Multiplex RT-qPCR revealed concurrent circulation of multiple arboviruses. Among individually tested samples, positivity rates were 20·9% (9/43) for DENV, 9·3% (4/43) for ZIKV, and 11·6% (5/43) for CHIKV. In pooled screening across all sites (108 pools), positivity rates were 18·5% for DENV (20/108), 5·6% for ZIKV (6/108), and 10·2% for CHIKV (11/108), indicating widespread arboviral transmission. DENV-1-4 serotyping by RT-RPA demonstrated complete concordance with RT-qPCR and identified exclusive circulation of DENV-2, enabling triage of samples for downstream genomic sequencing. Amplicon-based sequencing substantially improved genome recovery compared with metagenomic sequencing, yielding near-complete genomes in 77·8% (14/18) of RT-RPA-positive samples. Phylogenetic analyses demonstrated that all sequences clustered within the DENV-2 cosmopolitan genotype (genotype II), lineage II-F.1.1, closely related to recent strains from West Africa and Asia. Time-resolved reconstruction suggested recent emergence (∼2022-2023) and rapid expansion, consistent with ongoing transmission and regional dissemination. INTERPRETATION: These findings demonstrate co-circulation of DENV, ZIKV, and CHIKV in Senegal and provide evidence of recent expansion of DENV-2 within a globally connected transmission network. A tiered strategy integrating pooled molecular screening with RT-RPA triage and genomic sequencing offers a scalable framework for arboviral surveillance in resource-limited settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a tiered molecular surveillance framework for arboviruses in Senegal, focusing on dengue virus (DENV) and its co-circulation with Zika (ZIKV) and chikungunya (CHIKV) viruses. The research aimed to address the limitations of fragmented diagnostic capacity and the lack of integration between molecular detection and genomic epidemiology in Africa. A combination of multiplex RT-qPCR screening, RT-RPA serotyping, and genomic sequencing was used to analyze 367 samples, revealing concurrent circulation of DENV, ZIKV, and CHIKV. Positivity rates for DENV were higher than for ZIKV and CHIKV in both individually tested and pooled samples, indicating widespread transmission. The results showed that all DENV-2 sequences clustered within the cosmopolitan genotype II, lineage II-F.1.1, and were closely related to recent strains from West Africa and Asia. These findings suggest recent emergence and rapid expansion of DENV-2 within a globally connected transmission network, highlighting the need for improved surveillance strategies. The study's tiered approach, which combines pooled screening with RT-RPA triage and genomic sequencing, offers a scalable framework for arboviral surveillance in resource-limited settings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 非洲的虫媒病毒 监测 受到诊断能力分散以及分子检测与基因组 流行病学 整合不足的限制,特别是在登革热 (DENV)、寨卡病毒 (ZIKV) 和基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 病毒共同传播并出现重叠临床综合征的环境中。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们在塞内加尔的多个地区进行了一项分子 监测 研究,包括从 367 名发热或非发热疾病患者收集的样本。
elements_zh.methods: 使用针对 DENV、ZIKV 和 CHIKV 的多重逆转录定量聚合酶链反应 (RT-qPCR) 筛选来实施分层工作流程,对单独测试的样本 (n=43) 和合并样本(每个池三个个体)进行组合。通过逆转录重组酶聚合酶扩增 (RT-RPA) 血清分型和基因组测序进一步表征 DENV RT-qPCR 阳性样本。
elements_zh.main_results: 多重 RT-qPCR 显示多种虫媒病毒同时循环。在单独检测的样本中,DENV 阳性率为 20·9% (9/43),ZIKV 阳性率为 9·3% (4/43),CHIKV 阳性率为 11·6% (5/43)。在所有中心(108 个池)的汇总筛查中,DENV 阳性率为 18·5% (20/108),ZIKV 阳性率为 5·6% (6/108),CHIKV 阳性率为 10·2% (11/108),表明虫媒病毒 传播 广泛存在。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现证明了 DENV、ZIKV 和 CHIKV 在塞内加尔的共同传播,并提供了 DENV-2 最近在全球连接的 传播 网络中扩张的证据。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了DENV-2最近出现和快速扩张的证据,这可以为塞内加尔和其他具有类似虫媒病毒动态的地区的有针对性的监测、诊断和公共卫生干预措施提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 将汇总分子筛选与 RT-RPA 分类和基因组测序相结合的分层策略为资源有限环境中的虫媒病毒 监测 提供了可扩展的框架。

Among individually tested samples, positivity rates were 20·9% (9/43) for DENV, 9·3% (4/43) for ZIKV, and 11·6% (5/43) for CHIKV. In pooled screening across all sites (108 pools), positivity rates were 18·5% for DENV (20/108), 5·6% for ZIKV (6/108), and 10·2% for CHIKV (11/108), indicating widespread arboviral transmission. DENV-1-4 serotyping by RT-RPA demonstrated complete concordance with RT-qPCR and identified exclusive circulation of DENV-2, enabling triage of samples for downstream genomic sequencing. Amplicon-based sequencing substantially improved genome recovery compared with metagenomic sequencing, yielding near-complete genomes in 77·8% (14/18) of RT-RPA-positive samples. Phylogenetic analyses demonstrated that all sequences clustered within the DENV-2 cosmopolitan genotype (genotype II), lineage II-F.1.1, closely related to recent strains from West Africa and Asia. Time-resolved reconstruction suggested recent emergence (∼2022-2023) and rapid expansion, consistent with ongoing transmission and regional dissemination. INTERPRETATION: These findings demonstrate co-circulation of DENV, ZIKV, and CHIKV in Senegal and provide evidence of recent expansion of DENV-2 within a globally connected transmission network. A tiered strategy integrating pooled molecular screening with RT-RPA triage and genomic sequencing offers a scalable framework for arboviral surveillance in resource-limited settings.

title: Broadly cross-reactive neutralizing and enhancing antibody responses to dengue, Japanese encephalitis viruses and Zika in sera from Vietnamese pediatric dengue cases.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Understanding the balance between protective and pathogenic antibody responses is central to dengue immunology and flavivirus vaccine development. METHODS: Fifty paired acute and convalescent serum samples from pediatric dengue patients in southern Vietnam (2015-2017) were analyzed, including primary and secondary infections across a spectrum of disease severity. Primary and secondary DENV infections were classified using an in-house validated DENV IgG ELISA. Neutralizing antibody (NAb) titers and antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) activities were evaluated against dengue virus the four serotypes (DENV), Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) and ZIKA (ZIKV) using single-round infectious particles (SRIPs). RESULTS: Neutralizing antibody (NAb) responses were detected against all DENV serotypes and were highest against DENV-1. NAb titers increased during convalescence and were generally higher in secondary than primary infections. Higher NAb titers were also observed in convalescent sera from DSS cases compared with other clinical groups. ADE activity was most pronounced against DENV-2 and was lowest against DENV-4, while Peak enhancement titers (PET) were higher in convalescent samples, secondary infections, and DSS cases, and were positively correlated with NAb titers. Additionally, higher enhancement activity was observed in sera from DSS cases than in those from milder disease categories. Cross-reactive neutralizing and enhancing antibodies against JEV and ZIKV were also detected, with stronger enhancement observed against ZIKV. CONCLUSION: Heightened neutralizing immunity in secondary and severe dengue is accompanied by expanded enhancement potential, indicating an expanded, cross-reactive immune response driven by immune activation upon infection. The coexistence of protective and enhancing antibodies may contribute both to viral control and to immunopathogenesis during subsequent flavivirus infections.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the balance between neutralizing and enhancing antibody responses in pediatric dengue patients in southern Vietnam. It analyzes 50 paired serum samples from 2015-2017, including primary and secondary infections across varying disease severities. The research employs an in-house validated DENV IgG ELISA to classify infections and evaluates neutralizing antibody (NAb) titers and antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) activities against DENV serotypes, Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), and Zika virus (ZIKV) using single-round infectious particles (SRIPs). The results show that NAb responses are highest against DENV-1 and increase during convalescence, with secondary infections and severe dengue cases exhibiting higher titers. ADE activity is most pronounced against DENV-2 and lowest against DENV-4, with peak enhancement titers (PET) correlating with NAb levels. Sera from severe dengue cases (DSS) demonstrate higher enhancement activity compared to milder cases. Cross-reactive antibodies against JEV and ZIKV are also detected, with stronger enhancement observed against ZIKV. The authors conclude that heightened neutralizing immunity in secondary and severe dengue is associated with expanded enhancement potential, suggesting an activated immune response. They also propose that the coexistence of protective and enhancing antibodies may influence both viral control and immunopathogenesis during subsequent flavivirus infections. The study's findings may contribute to the development of more effective dengue vaccines and improve understanding of immune responses in severe cases. However, the study is limited to a specific geographic and demographic population, which may affect generalizability, and the evidence is based on abstract-only data, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title_zh: 广泛交叉反应中和并增强越南儿童登革热病例血清中对登革热、日本脑炎病毒和寨卡病毒的抗体反应。

The coexistence of protective and enhancing antibodies may contribute both to viral control and to immunopathogenesis during subsequent flavivirus infections.

title: Prevalence and factors associated with dengue fever serotypes in Eastern Sudan: a hospital-based cross-sectional study
abstract: Dengue is a critical public health threat in Sudan, exacerbated by rapid urbanization and climatic factors. The 2024 outbreak in Kassala State occurred amidst a violent internal conflict and massive population displacement, synergistically accelerating transmission and complicating clinical management. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of dengue virus (DENV) serotypes and identify sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with specific serotypes among residents and internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Kassala during the 2024 epidemic. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted at Kassala Teaching Hospital (October–December 2024). Serum samples from 227 confirmed dengue patients (RDT-positive for NS1, IgM, or both) were analyzed using one-step Real-Time PCR for serotyping. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with the most prevalent serotypes. Among the confirmed 227 dengue fever, DENV-2 was the dominant serotype (59.9%), followed by DENV-3 (35.2%) and DENV-1 (4.8%). Notably, 52% of patients were IDPs, and 30.4% presented with severe forms (DHF/DSS). The overall mortality rate was 6.6%, with 13 out of the 15 recorded deaths occurring among the displaced population. While a high fatality rate was noted among the small subset of DENV-1 patients (4 out of 11), this finding must be interpreted with extreme caution due to the limited sample size. Multivariate analysis revealed that the non-use of mosquito nets was the only independent factor associated with DENV-2 infection (adjusted odds ratio, AOR = 2.20; 95% CI: 1.23–3.90; P = 0.007). No significant differences were found between serotypes regarding age, gender, or displacement status. The 2024 dengue outbreak marked a significant shift from DENV-3 to DENV-2 dominance, with a high mortality burden clustering heavily within vulnerable IDPs due to systemic displacement factors rather than strain dominance. The strong association between net non-use and DENV-2 highlights the urgent need for targeted long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) distribution and vector control in displacement camps. Additionally, the high fatality rate in the small DENV-1 subset underscores the necessity of strengthened molecular surveillance to monitor virulent strains in conflict zones.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热是苏丹的一个严重的公共卫生威胁,快速城市化和气候因素加剧了这一威胁。本研究旨在确定 登革病毒 (DENV) 血清型的 患病率,并确定 2024 年流行期间卡萨拉居民和境内流离失所者 (IDP) 中与特定血清型相关的社会人口学和临床因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 卡萨拉教学医院进行了一项以医院为基础的横断面研究(2024 年 10 月至 12 月)。在确诊的 227 例 登革热 病例中,52% 的患者为境内流离失所者,30.4% 为重症(DHF/DSS)。
elements_zh.methods: 使用一步实时 PCR 分析 227 名确诊登革热患者(NS1、IgM 或两者均呈 RDT 阳性)的血清样本进行血清分型。进行单变量和多变量逻辑回归分析以确定与最流行血清型相关的因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 在确诊的227例登革热病例中,DENV-2是主要血清型(59.9%),其次是DENV-3(35.2%)和DENV-1(4.8%)。总体 死亡率 率为 6.6%,记录的 15 例死亡中有 13 例发生在流离失所者中。多变量分析显示,不使用蚊帐是与 DENV-2 感染相关的唯一独立因素(调整优势比,AOR = 2.20;95% CI:1.23–3.90;P = 0.007)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 2024 年登革热 暴发 标志着从 DENV-3 到 DENV-2 主导地位的重大转变,由于系统性流离失所因素而不是毒株主导,高 死亡率 负担严重集中在易受伤害的国内流离失所者中。不使用蚊帐与 DENV-2 之间的密切关联凸显了在流离失所者营地中迫切需要有针对性地分发长效杀虫蚊帐 (LLIN) 和 媒介 控制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: DENV-1 小型亚群的高死亡率强调了加强分子 监测 来监测冲突地区毒力菌株的必要性。此外,研究结果强调需要采取有针对性的 媒介 控制措施,以减少高危人群中的登革热 传播。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于样本量有限,必须极其谨慎地解释一小部分 DENV-1 患者的高死亡率。证据强度中等,因为该研究为 患病率 血清型和相关因素提供了有价值的见解,但受到其横断面设计和某些血清型样本量较小的限制。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: DENV-1 小型亚群的高死亡率强调了加强分子 监测 来监测冲突地区毒力菌株的必要性。此外,研究结果强调需要采取有针对性的 媒介 控制措施,以减少高危人群中的登革热 传播。

title: Optimal Control Analysis and Cost – Effectiveness of Dengue Transmission Model Along With Implementation Time Effects in Applying the Control Interventions
abstract: ABSTRACT Dengue fever poses a significant global public health threat, and its effective management requires a comprehensive approach to control the dengue prevalence. This study proposes an optimal control problem for the dengue transmission, incorporating three key control measures: information‐induced self‐protection, saturated treatment, and pesticide use for vector control, and is analyzed using Pontryagin's Maximum Principle. Importantly, a novel higher nonlinearity in the cost construction is incorporated. Seven distinct control policies () incorporating different combinations of control measures are designed and evaluated through numerical simulations. The results demonstrate that the combined strategy of all controls (Policy ) is the most effective, reducing infection prevalence to minimal levels within approximately 60 days, while maintaining sustained control thereafter. In comparison, the combined use of information and treatment (Policy ) achieves a similar outcome but requires nearly 120 days to stabilize the infection. Among single‐control strategies, information‐induced self‐protection (Policy ) outperforms treatment () and pesticide application () when applied alone. Cost‐effectiveness analysis using CCER, IAR, and ICER reveals that Policy is the most cost‐effective intervention, with the lowest CCER value, while Policy averts the highest number of infections. Furthermore, the analysis shows that the control's effectiveness depends strongly on epidemic severity: for mild outbreaks (), combined strategies such as and (treatment and pesticide) perform efficiently, whereas for severe outbreaks (), comprehensive control () becomes essential. Additionally, delayed implementation of control measures significantly worsens disease outcomes, increasing infection peaks and economic burden. Overall, the study highlights the importance of timely and integrated intervention strategies and provides quantitative insights for optimal resource allocation in dengue control.

title: Dengue outbreak investigation in Mfandena I Health Area, Cameroon, 2025: Evidence of Aedes vectors and routine surveillance gaps
abstract: Introduction: In December 2024, a sudden increase in dengue cases was reported in Mfandena I health area (HA), Yaounde, Cameroon. Two confirmed cases that escaped routine surveillance were notified, and little data were available. A multidisciplinary team was deployed to conduct active case-finding, identify potential vectors and their larval habitats, and evaluate the dengue surveillance system. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study in January 2025 (dry season) in Mfandena I HA. Cases were identified through healthcare records reviews and community screening. Suspected cases were people living in Mfandena I HA with fever >38.5°C lasting 2-7 days and at least two of the following symptoms: headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, arthralgia, skin rash, hemorrhagic manifestations since November 2024. Immunoglobulin M (IgM) and non-structural protein 1 (NS1) tests were carried out on consenting suspected cases and their contacts. An entomological survey was conducted within a 1 km radius around the case residences. We followed the CDC framework combined with the WHO IDSR approach for surveillance system evaluation. Results: We identified 46 dengue cases (44 suspected cases and 02 confirmed cases) and 16 contacts, but no additional cases were confirmed. Dengue cases were mostly women aged 21 years or older, with fever, arthralgia, and headache as main symptoms. The confirmed cases were male adults: one residing in Cameroon and one arriving from France, both presenting with fever and a red-spot rash. Among 143 Aedes mosquitoes collected, Ae. albopictus accounted for 88% (126/143). We detected a discarded tyre containing Ae. albopictus larvae as the likely source of infection. The surveillance system exhibited gaps in detection and reporting and was neither simple, acceptable, nor stable. Only 16% (4/25) of staff were familiar with the case definition, no sites had notification forms, and no cases had ever been reported. Conclusion: This investigation suggests potential dengue transmission in Mfandena I HA and highlights important surveillance gaps that limited timely detection and reporting. Strengthening surveillance capacity and reinforcing routine entomological investigations are essential to improve outbreak detection, response and prevention.
